Reporting to the Executive Director of Global Programs, the Associate Director works closely with the Executive Director on all operational aspects of the UCI Law’s Master of Laws Program (LL.M.) for internationally trained attorneys. Responsibilities include recruitment and admissions, academic advising, career counseling, student orientation, and LL.M. events.

Recruitment and Admissions: Will represent UCI Law by participating in virtual and in-person law fairs/graduate school fairs in Europe, South America and Asia, with travel from mid- September through November and occasional travel thereafter. Working closely with the Executive Director of Global Programs, the candidate will research, develop, and implement programs and marketing initiatives designed to maximize the Law School's ability to enroll the most highly qualified LL.M. candidates, including the planning and management of outreach initiatives. This includes implementing strategies to recruit diverse and talented applicants and developing, directly advising LL.M. students on course enrollment, professional development, orientation and bar admission, and updating programmatic materials for the international LL.M. student population.

Academic Advising: Directly counsel current and prospective LL.M. students – individually and in groups - on course selection and degree requirements, bar admission for LL.M.s, professional development/career matters and cultural orientation issues. Advise management on a variety of student issues.

Career Counseling: Advises LL.M. students on the job market process; develops and presents professional development workshops (resumes, cover letters, job interview skills, etc.); develops and maintains network of regional firms, bar associations, and organizations interested in networking, mentorship, employment, and other professional development opportunities for LL.M. students; communicates with and engages LL.M. alumni to foster community and mentorship between former and current students.
Student Orientation and LL.M. Events: Plan and oversee major program events, including Orientation and workshops on spring registration
Working knowledge of advising and counseling technique
